headline: Roivant: first drug launch brings $31 million in five weeks, and three clinical wins in one quarter; $4.2 billion of cash
takeaway: LISRAYA (brepocitinib) earned $31.0 million in its first five weeks after FDA approval for dermatomyositis, and the loss narrowed to $0.18 a share, far better than the $0.45 expected. IMVT-1402 succeeded in a difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis trial, brepocitinib won two Phase 3 uveitis trials, and the shares rose 4.6%.
results: Roivant reported revenue of $35.1 million for its fiscal second quarter, ended September 30, against $1.6 million a year earlier, almost all of it from LISRAYA, which generated $31.0 million of net product revenue in its first five weeks on the US market following FDA approval in August for adult dermatomyositis, a rare inflammatory muscle and skin disease. The net loss per share narrowed to $0.18 from $0.28.

Brepocitinib, a JAK1 and TYK2 inhibitor, met the primary and all key secondary endpoints in the Phase 3 CLARITY-1 and CLARITY-2 trials in non-infectious uveitis, an inflammatory eye disease; a supplemental application is expected in the first half of 2027. Mosliciguat produced positive Phase 2 data in pulmonary hypertension associated with interstitial lung disease, and a Phase 3 trial has begun.

Immunovant’s IMVT-1402, an FcRn antibody, met its primary endpoint at the 600 mg dose in a potentially registrational trial in difficult-to-treat rheumatoid arthritis: 92.5% of patients kept an ACR20 response at week 28 against 75.6% on placebo. Roivant ended the quarter with $4.2 billion of cash and securities, including a payment from Moderna received in July.
mgmt: Chief executive Matt Gline called it a major transition for Roivant, with LISRAYA commercially available and off to a strong start reflecting patient and prescriber demand, and said IMVT-1402’s data support its potential to maintain and deepen responses in patients who have failed multiple advanced therapies. Roivant plans FDA discussions later this year on the registration path for IMVT-1402 in rheumatoid arthritis.

The company said that, given the evolving landscape and recent data in Sjögren’s disease, it is unlikely to advance IMVT-1402 in that indication beyond the current Phase 2 trial. It said its cash supports a runway into profitability and will hold an investor day on December 9.
view: Roivant has spent a decade as a drug-development holding company, spinning out subsidiaries, selling assets — most famously its anti-TL1A antibody to Roche for more than $7 billion — and recycling the proceeds. This quarter it became a commercial company. $31 million in five weeks is a strong launch for a rare-disease drug: annualised, that pace is already above $300 million, and dermatomyositis patients have few effective oral options. The uveitis data add a second, larger indication within about eighteen months.

The IMVT-1402 result is good but nuanced. A randomised-withdrawal design, where all patients first receive the drug and responders are then randomised to continue or switch to placebo, tends to flatter results, and the 17-point gap is meaningful rather than overwhelming. FcRn drugs have also had a mixed run — the decision to drop Sjögren’s reflects disappointing data across the class. Still, rheumatoid arthritis patients who have failed several therapies are a large, underserved group, and a clean path with the FDA would make IMVT-1402 a major asset.

What makes Roivant unusual among biotech companies is the balance sheet. With $4.2 billion of cash against a market value of about $28 billion and a stated runway to profitability, it can fund three late-stage programmes without diluting shareholders, and the Moderna payment from the lipid-nanoparticle patent dispute shows its legal assets also have value. The risk is that the valuation already assumes several of these programmes succeed; the LISRAYA launch trajectory over the next two quarters will be the clearest test of whether Roivant can sell drugs as well as it develops them.
watch: Watch LISRAYA prescriptions and revenue in the December quarter, the FDA meeting on IMVT-1402 in rheumatoid arthritis, the uveitis filing in 2027 and plans for the cash at the December investor day.
